headline: FAA NOTAM outage triggers a nationwide US ground stop
significance: A critical information-system failure temporarily halted domestic departures across the United States.
summary: The FAA ordered airlines to pause domestic departures while it restored the Notice to Air Missions system. A preliminary review later traced the outage to files unintentionally deleted during database synchronization work.

headline: Air India agrees to order 220 Boeing aircraft
significance: The commitment became a central part of Air India’s fleet renewal under Tata Group ownership.
summary: Air India agreed to firm orders for 190 Boeing 737 Max aircraft, 20 787s and 10 777Xs. The wide-ranging order supported plans to expand both domestic and long-haul operations.

headline: EASA publishes its 2023 Annual Safety Review
significance: The review fed observed risks into Europe’s continuing aviation-safety planning process.
summary: The review assessed European aviation safety performance during 2022 as traffic recovered from the pandemic. EASA said its analysis supports decisions and mitigations incorporated into the European Plan for Aviation Safety.

headline: Global passenger traffic returns to 94.1% of 2019 levels
significance: The industry moved close to completing its post-pandemic demand recovery.
summary: IATA reported that total passenger traffic rose 36.9% in 2023 and reached 94.1% of the 2019 level. Domestic traffic finished above its 2019 level while international traffic remained below it.

headline: FAA grounds certain Boeing 737-9 Max aircraft
significance: The order affected about 171 aircraft worldwide following the Alaska Airlines door-plug event.
summary: The FAA required immediate inspections of affected Boeing 737-9 Max aircraft before further flight. The action followed the rapid decompression event involving Alaska Airlines Flight 1282 on January 5.

headline: IATA raises its 2024 airline profitability outlook
significance: The updated forecast pointed to record traveller numbers and revenues despite thin margins.
summary: IATA forecast a $30.5 billion aggregate airline net profit for 2024 and nearly five billion travellers. It also warned that returns remained below the industry’s average cost of capital.

headline: Boeing and Airbus agree to divide Spirit AeroSystems operations
significance: The transaction reshaped a major aerospace supplier amid intense scrutiny of manufacturing quality.
summary: Boeing confirmed an agreement to acquire Spirit AeroSystems, including net debt, while Airbus prepared to acquire programmes supporting its aircraft. Spirit was a major supplier to both manufacturers.

headline: Vistara begins operating as part of Air India
significance: The merger consolidated Tata Group’s full-service airline operations under the Air India brand.
summary: Vistara’s operations moved into Air India following the long-planned merger. The combination expanded Air India’s domestic and international network and brought together two full-service fleets.

headline: FAA and EASA renew their civil-aviation safety partnership
significance: The declaration reinforced transatlantic cooperation on safe and secure civil aviation.
summary: FAA and EASA signed a Declaration of Intent during ICAO’s 80th-anniversary events. The agencies committed to continue and deepen their safety and security cooperation.

headline: Passenger jet and US Army helicopter collide near Washington National
significance: The fatal accident prompted urgent scrutiny of airspace design and helicopter operations near DCA.
summary: A PSA Airlines CRJ700 operating as American Airlines Flight 5342 collided with a US Army UH-60L helicopter near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport. The NTSB opened a major investigation and later issued urgent safety recommendations.

headline: IATA forecasts modestly stronger airline profitability for 2025
significance: Record passenger load factors highlighted strong demand alongside aircraft supply constraints.
summary: IATA projected a $36 billion industry profit on $979 billion in revenue for 2025. The association expected an all-time-high average passenger load factor as airlines faced continuing fleet and maintenance constraints.

headline: ICAO recognises India’s progress in aviation safety oversight
significance: The recognition highlighted improvements in India’s implementation of international safety standards.
summary: DGCA received an ICAO Council President Certificate during the 42nd ICAO Assembly. DGCA said the certificate recognised India’s progress in effective safety oversight and implementation of ICAO standards and recommended practices.

headline: DGCA grants an aerodrome licence to Navi Mumbai International Airport
significance: The licence marked a key regulatory milestone for additional airport capacity in the Mumbai region.
summary: DGCA granted Navi Mumbai International Airport a code 4F aerodrome licence. The licensed configuration included a 3,700-metre runway and Category I instrument landing capability.

headline: EASA publishes its first ReFuelEU Aviation technical report
significance: The report established an early baseline for sustainable aviation fuel supply and use in the EU.
summary: EASA published the first annual technical assessment of ReFuelEU Aviation implementation. It covered stakeholder compliance data and emerging trends in sustainable aviation fuel supply, purchasing and use.

headline: EASA publishes the European Plan for Aviation Safety 2026
significance: The plan updated Europe’s shared safety priorities and mitigation actions.
summary: The 2026 edition added priorities covering big-data safety risk management, rule simplification and implementation of the Single European Sky framework. It also updated the European safety-risk portfolio.

headline: Air India receives its first factory-fresh Boeing 787-9
significance: The delivery advanced Air India’s widebody renewal and long-haul expansion programme.
summary: Air India took delivery of its first factory-fresh Boeing 787-9. The carrier also expected additional widebody deliveries, including its first Airbus A350-1000s, during the year.

headline: IATA reports record passenger demand and load factors for 2025
significance: Strong demand persisted while airlines continued to face aircraft, engine and maintenance constraints.
summary: IATA reported that 2025 passenger demand rose 5.3% and the industry load factor reached a record 83.6%. Domestic India recorded the highest full-year load factor among the domestic markets in the report.

headline: NTSB expands its civil aviation accident dashboard with findings data
significance: The change made investigation findings easier to explore alongside accident records.
summary: The NTSB enhanced its public civil aviation accident dashboard to include findings data. The agency retired its separate general aviation dashboard as part of the update.

headline: EASA assesses socio-economic factors affecting aviation safety
significance: The report examined whether employment and working conditions were linked to adverse safety outcomes.
summary: EASA published its second Article 89 report on the relationship between aviation safety and socio-economic factors affecting safety-critical personnel. The assessment did not identify a systemic causal relationship within its scope.

headline: EASA updates safety guidance on GNSS interference
significance: The update addressed an operational risk affecting navigation across multiple regions.
summary: EASA updated its Safety Information Bulletin concerning interference with global navigation satellite systems. The agency also continued joint work with EUROCONTROL on actions for safer operations during interference events.

headline: IndiGo and CFM outline an agreement for more than 1,000 LEAP-1A engines
significance: The proposed record engine agreement supports one of the world’s largest narrowbody fleet-growth programmes.
summary: IndiGo and CFM International signed an MoU covering LEAP-1A engines for 510 Airbus A320neo-family aircraft. It also includes support for an IndiGo engine maintenance, repair and overhaul facility in India.

headline: India begins international hub-and-spoke operations from Amritsar
significance: The initiative extended India’s international hub strategy to a second regional spoke airport.
summary: The Ministry of Civil Aviation inaugurated hub-and-spoke international passenger operations from Amritsar. The model enables through check-in and baggage connections via Delhi to a broader international network.

headline: Air India appoints Tewolde Gebremariam as CEO and Managing Director
significance: The appointment places an experienced airline turnaround leader in charge of Air India’s next expansion and execution phase.
summary: Air India’s board appointed Tewolde Gebremariam to succeed Campbell Wilson. Gebremariam previously led Ethiopian Airlines Group through a major expansion; Air India said his precise onboarding and transition schedule would follow.

headline: Air India Group begins a new phase of domestic network optimisation
significance: The changes started aligning routes between Air India and the newly acquired AirAsia India.
summary: The group reassigned selected stations and increased connections and frequencies on major domestic routes. Air India said the objective was to match routes with the most suitable full-service or low-cost operating model.

headline: Air India expands Dubai services from Delhi and Mumbai
significance: The schedule alignment with Air India Express strengthened one of the group’s largest international markets.
summary: Air India increased Delhi–Dubai service to as many as ten daily flights and Mumbai–Dubai to as many as six. The airline coordinated timings with Air India Express as part of group network alignment.

headline: Air India unveils a new global brand and aircraft livery
significance: The Vista identity became the public face of the airline’s post-privatisation transformation.
summary: Air India introduced a new logo, colour system and livery as part of Vihaan.AI. The airline said the identity would roll out alongside new digital products, aircraft and cabin interiors.

headline: Air India completes acquisition of its first A350-900 through GIFT IFSC
significance: The transaction advanced Air India’s widebody renewal and India’s aircraft-leasing ecosystem.
summary: Air India completed the finance-lease transaction for its first Airbus A350-900 through GIFT City. The aircraft was the first of six A350-900s due to join the carrier.

headline: Air India plans more than 400 additional weekly flights
significance: The expansion translated incoming aircraft into a materially larger domestic and international network.
summary: Air India outlined plans to add more than 200 weekly domestic flights and over 200 international flights by March 2024. It expected more than 30 aircraft to join during the six-month period.

headline: Air India starts rolling out its new identity across customer touchpoints
significance: The new brand moved from design announcement to operational deployment online, at airports and on aircraft.
summary: Air India switched its digital channels and selected airport touchpoints to the new identity. The airline linked the aircraft rollout to its incoming A350 fleet and planned cabin refurbishment programme.

headline: Air India launches a 600,000-square-foot aviation training academy
significance: The facility created training capacity for the airline group’s rapid fleet and workforce growth.
summary: Air India announced an integrated Gurugram academy with more than 20 planned full-flight simulator bays. It aimed to train over 50,000 aviation professionals across multiple disciplines.

headline: Air India’s first Airbus A350 enters passenger service
significance: The flight marked the commercial debut of the A350 in India and a visible step in Air India’s fleet renewal.
summary: Air India operated its first passenger A350 flight from Bengaluru to Mumbai. The aircraft was the first delivery from the carrier’s record-setting 470-aircraft order.

headline: Air India details the Vistara customer transition and AI2 flight codes
significance: The announcement explained how Vistara’s product and loyalty members would move into the enlarged Air India.
summary: Air India said former Vistara aircraft would retain their service proposition and use four-digit flight numbers beginning with AI2. Club Vistara accounts were scheduled to move into Maharaja Club.

headline: Air India concentrates upgraded narrowbody cabins on major metro routes
significance: The post-merger fleet plan used former Vistara aircraft to standardise a three-class product on high-frequency routes.
summary: Air India assigned its strongest narrowbody cabin products to five metro-to-metro markets. The schedule covered more than 1,000 weekly flights across the selected routes.

headline: Air India adds 100 Airbus aircraft to its firm orders
significance: The follow-on order deepened the group’s long-term commitment to fleet expansion after its 2023 megadeal.
summary: Air India added 10 A350 widebodies and 90 A320-family aircraft to its Airbus orderbook. The transaction increased its Airbus orders placed since 2023 to 350 aircraft.

headline: Air India becomes the first Indian airline to offer Wi-Fi on domestic flights
significance: The rollout introduced internet connectivity to selected domestic aircraft for the first time in India.
summary: Air India launched complimentary introductory Wi-Fi on A350s, Boeing 787-9s and selected A321neos. The service covered both domestic and international flights operated by those aircraft.

headline: Air India shifts Delhi–Tokyo flights to Haneda and expands its ANA codeshare
significance: The move improved access to central Tokyo and broadened onward connectivity within Japan.
summary: Air India moved its four weekly Delhi services from Narita to Haneda from 31 March 2025. An expanded ANA codeshare added connections to six other Japanese cities.

headline: Air India Flight AI171 crashes shortly after take-off from Ahmedabad
significance: The fatal Boeing 787 accident became the most consequential safety event in Air India’s recent history.
summary: Air India confirmed that the Ahmedabad–London Gatwick flight crashed shortly after departure with 242 people aboard. The airline established assistance centres, supported affected families and cooperated with the official investigation.

headline: Air India begins restoring international schedules after its safety pause
significance: The partial restoration followed additional Boeing 787 checks and temporary network reductions after AI171.
summary: Air India announced phased frequency restorations from August, with full restoration planned for October. Some routes remained reduced while operating and airspace constraints continued.

headline: Air India adds a Scoot interline partnership across Asia and Australasia
significance: The agreement extended Air India’s accessible network through Singapore to more than 60 destinations.
summary: The unilateral interline partnership enabled single-ticket connections and through check-in across much of Scoot’s network. It added destinations not covered by Air India’s existing partnerships.

headline: Air India announces its return to Rome after nearly six years
significance: The planned service restored another major European destination to Air India’s network.
summary: Air India scheduled four weekly Delhi–Rome flights from 25 March 2026. The timings were designed to connect Italy with destinations across India and Southeast Asia via Delhi.

headline: Air India converts 15 A321neo orders to the A321XLR
significance: The longer-range narrowbody option creates scope for new medium-haul international routes.
summary: Air India converted 15 existing Airbus A321neo orders to the A321XLR, with deliveries expected in 2029 and 2030. The airline cited the type’s range and single-aisle economics.

headline: Air India and Lufthansa Group establish a joint-business framework
significance: The MoU opened the path to deeper commercial coordination between India and major European markets.
summary: The carriers agreed to explore coordinated schedules, sales, distribution and customer-experience initiatives. Any comprehensive joint business remains subject to regulatory and antitrust approvals.

headline: Air India announces Campbell Wilson’s resignation
significance: The announcement initiated a leadership transition after the airline’s initial post-privatisation integration phase.
summary: Air India said Wilson would remain CEO and Managing Director until a successor was announced and in place. The airline highlighted the merger, systems and fleet work completed during his tenure.

headline: Air India and SIA Engineering explore an Indian MRO partnership
significance: The agreement supports Air India’s effort to build more maintenance capability within India.
summary: Air India and SIA Engineering signed an MoU to examine deeper maintenance, repair and overhaul collaboration. The potential arrangement could include an MRO joint venture in India.

headline: Air India and Saudia agree to expand strategic cooperation
significance: The MoU broadened a partnership serving the fast-growing India–Saudi Arabia market.
summary: The airlines agreed to explore wider codesharing, improved connections, terminal co-location and loyalty cooperation. The framework could later extend to other airlines within both groups.

headline: Air India expands Canada service and deploys its new 787-9 to Toronto
significance: The changes increased India–Canada capacity while introducing Air India’s newest long-haul cabin product.
summary: Air India launched a seasonal Mumbai–Toronto service for winter 2026–27 and deployed a new Boeing 787-9 on Delhi–Toronto. The airline projected 4,400 additional seats per month between India and Canada.
